matrices.title: Exotoxin vs. Endotoxin
matrices.summary: High-yield side-by-side contrast between secreted bacterial protein exotoxins and outer-membrane lipopolysaccharide endotoxins.
rows: Bacterial Source
Secreted by both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria [L5 p15]
Integral component of the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria ONLY [L1 p20, 23, L5 p25]
Chemical Composition
Polypeptide / Protein [L5 p15]
Lipopolysaccharide complex (toxic moiety is Lipid A) [L1 p23, L5 p25]
Gene Location
Often encoded on extrachromosomal plasmids or lysogenic temperate bacteriophages [L2 p8, 22]
Encoded by stable bacterial chromosomal genes required for cell envelope structure [L1 p23]
Toxicity & Lethality
Extremely potent; lethal in microgram or nanogram amounts (e.g., botulinum toxin is the most lethal poison known) [L5 p15, 17]
Moderately toxic; lethal dose is much higher (milligram amounts) [L5 p25]
Heat Stability
Heat-labile: Rapidly destroyed at 60°C (major exception: staphylococcal enterotoxin is heat-stable) [L5 p15, 19]
Heat-stable: Readily withstands 100°C boiling for 1 hour without loss of activity [L1 p23, L5 p25]
Toxoid & Vaccine Feasibility
Highly immunogenic; can be detoxified with formaldehyde to form non-toxic **toxoids** used in vaccines (e.g., tetanus and diphtheria toxoids) [L5 p24]
Weakly immunogenic; CANNOT be converted into toxoids; no effective toxoid vaccines exist [L5 p25]
Receptor & Action Mechanism
Binds specific host cell surface receptors; acts via specialized enzymatic mechanisms (e.g., ADP-ribosylation of EF-2, cleavage of SNAREs, superantigens) [L5 p16-22]
Binds CD14/TLR4 on macrophages to trigger massive systemic release of endogenous cytokines: **IL-1, TNF-alpha, Nitric Oxide, PAF** [L1 p23, L5 p25]
Clinical Manifestations
Specific disease syndromes based on target tissue: Spastic paralysis (tetanus), flaccid paralysis (botulism), rice-water diarrhea (cholera), diphtheritic membrane [L5 p17-22]
Non-specific systemic manifestations: High fever (IL-1), septic shock and hypotension (TNF), disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC via tissue factor) [L1 p23, L5 p25]

matrices.title: Mechanisms of Horizontal Gene Transfer
matrices.summary: Comparison of Transformation, Conjugation, and Transduction in bacterial genetic recombination.
rows: Transformation [L2 p14]
Uptake of free, naked DNA from the extracellular environment by 'competent' recipient cells [L2 p14]
**Sensitive to DNase** (extracellular deoxyribonuclease degrades free DNA in the medium and aborts transfer) [L2 p14]
Griffith experiment; natural competence in Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria, and Haemophilus; transfer of capsule and penicillin-binding protein genes [L2 p14, 15]
Conjugation [L2 p16]
Direct cell-to-cell contact mediated by a **sex pilus**; F factor (plasmid) transfers a single strand via rolling circle replication from F+ donor to F- recipient [L2 p7, 16]
**Resistant to DNase** (transferred DNA passes directly through a protected intercellular cytoplasmic bridge) [L2 p16]
Primary mechanism for rapid epidemic spread of multi-drug resistance plasmids (R factors) among Enterobacteriaceae; Hfr strains transfer chromosomal genes [L2 p8, 17, 27]
Transduction (Generalized) [L2 p20]
Accidental packaging of random fragments of host bacterial chromosomal DNA into a **lytic bacteriophage** capsid during assembly [L2 p20]
**Resistant to DNase** (transferred DNA is shielded inside the viral protein capsid) [L2 p20]
Transfers any bacterial gene at low frequency; mediated by virulent or temperate phages; does not require cell-to-cell contact [L2 p20, 21]
Transduction (Specialized) [L2 p22]
Faulty excision of an integrated **temperate (lysogenic) prophage** from the host chromosome, carrying adjacent flanking bacterial genes [L2 p22]
**Resistant to DNase** (transferred DNA is inside viral capsid) [L2 p22]
**Lysogenic conversion**: Acquisition of potent exotoxin genes (Diphtheria toxin in Corynebacterium, Botulinum toxin C/D, Cholera toxin in Vibrio, Shiga-like toxin in E. coli, SpeA in GAS) [L2 p22]

matrices.title: Gram-Positive vs. Gram-Negative Cell Wall Architecture
matrices.summary: Structural, biochemical, and pharmacological distinctions between Gram-positive and Gram-negative envelopes.
rows: Peptidoglycan Layer
Thick, multi-layered sacculus (up to 40 layers, 20-80 nm); highly cross-linked by pentaglycine peptide bridges [L1 p15, 25]
Thin, single- or double-layered sheet (1-2 layers, 1-3 nm); directly cross-linked between D-alanine and diaminopimelic acid [L1 p15, 25]
Outer Membrane
**Absent** [L1 p15]
**Present**: Asymmetric lipid bilayer (inner leaflet phospholipids, outer leaflet lipopolysaccharide) [L1 p15, 20]
Lipopolysaccharide (LPS / Endotoxin)
**Absent** [L1 p15]
**Present** in outer leaflet: Composed of Lipid A (toxic domain), Core polysaccharide, and O-antigen repeat units [L1 p20, 23]
Teichoic & Lipoteichoic Acids
**Present**: Ribitol or glycerol phosphate polymers; wall teichoic acids covalent to peptidoglycan; lipoteichoic acids anchor in cytoplasmic membrane; induce TNF and IL-1 (sepsis) [L1 p21, 27]
**Absent** entirely [L1 p15, 27]
Periplasmic Space
Narrow or virtually absent [L1 p15]
**Prominent gel-filled space** between inner and outer membranes; contains **beta-lactamases**, transport proteins, and nutrient-processing enzymes [L1 p16, 18]
Porin Channels
**Absent** (nutrients diffuse directly through porous peptidoglycan mesh) [L1 p19]
**Present**: Trimeric protein channels spanning outer membrane; regulate passage of hydrophilic molecules and antibiotics [L1 p19]
Susceptibility to Lysozyme
**Highly sensitive**: Lysozyme hydrolyzes beta-1,4 glycosidic bond between NAM and NAG, forming osmotic protoplasts [L1 p36]
**Low sensitivity**: Outer membrane shields peptidoglycan from lysozyme unless membrane is first permeabilized with EDTA [L1 p36]
Susceptibility to Penicillins
Generally high susceptibility to natural penicillins (e.g. Penicillin G) if non-beta-lactamase producing [L1 p31]
Naturally more resistant due to outer membrane barrier and periplasmic beta-lactamase localization [L1 p16, 31]

matrices.title: Physical and Chemical Methods of Microbial Control
matrices.summary: Sterilization, disinfection, and antisepsis parameters tested in medical microbiology.
rows: Steam Under Pressure (Autoclave) [L1 p53, L3 p41]
**121°C at 15 pounds per square inch (psi) pressure for 15-20 minutes** [L1 p53, L3 p41]
Denatures and coagulates microbial structural proteins and essential enzymes; penetrates spores rapidly [L1 p53]
**Gold-standard sterilization**: Kills all vegetative cells and resistant endospores (biological indicator: Geobacillus stearothermophilus spores) [L1 p53]
Dry Heat (Hot Air Oven) [L3 p42]
**160°C to 170°C for 2 hours** [L3 p42]
Oxidation of cellular constituents and thermal protein denaturation [L3 p42]
Used for dry glassware, metal instruments, and anhydrous oils/powders that cannot tolerate moisture [L3 p42]
Membrane Filtration [L3 p44]
**0.22 micrometer pore-size filters** [L3 p44]
Physical retention/exclusion of bacterial cells based on size [L3 p44]
Sterilizes heat-labile liquids (e.g., intravenous fluids, antibiotic solutions, serum, enzyme preparations); does NOT remove viruses [L3 p44]
Alcohols (70% Ethyl / Isopropyl) [L3 p46]
**70% aqueous concentration** (more bactericidal than 100% absolute alcohol because water facilitates protein denaturation) [L3 p46]
Disrupts lipid membrane integrity and coagulates proteins [L3 p46]
**Antiseptic**: Skin disinfection prior to venipuncture; does NOT kill bacterial endospores [L1 p53, L3 p46]

matrices.title: Bacterial Endospores vs. Vegetative Cells
matrices.summary: Key structural, physiological, and chemical differences between dormant endospores and active vegetative bacteria.
rows: Metabolic State
Completely metabolically dormant; zero detectable enzymatic respiration or macromolecular synthesis [L1 p52]
Metabolically active; continuous replication, protein synthesis, and nutrient uptake [L1 p12, L3 p4]
Calcium Dipicolinate Content
**High** (calcium dipicolinate constitutes up to 10-15% of spore dry weight; chelates calcium to dehydrate core) [L1 p52]
**Absent** entirely [L1 p52]
Water Content
Extremely low core hydration (10% to 25% water content); gel-like consistency protects DNA from heat denaturation [L1 p52]
High hydration (75% to 80% water content) [L1 p12]
Resistance to Heat & Boiling
Remarkably heat-resistant; survives 100°C boiling for hours; killed only by pressurized steam autoclaving at 121°C for 15-20 min [L1 p53]
Heat-sensitive; killed by boiling or pasteurization (60-65°C for 30 minutes) [L1 p53, L3 p41]
Resistance to Chemicals & Radiation
Highly resistant to disinfectants, drying, organic solvents, and UV/ionizing radiation due to thick keratin-like spore coat [L1 p52, 53]
Sensitive to standard disinfectants (alcohols, phenols, halogens) and drying [L3 p46]
Genera Capable of Sporulation
**Only two medically important genera**: Bacillus (aerobic) and Clostridium (anaerobic) [L1 p52, L3 p14]
All bacterial genera [L1 p8]
